# SPARK — Monorepo Root

This repository is an **assembly monorepo**: it bundles the source repositories of the SPARK API project into a single, navigable tree for public collaboration. Each subdirectory is a self-contained sub-repository with its own README, tests, and configuration.

## Repository Structure

```
.
├── 01-frontend/          # Micro-frontend shell + all MFEs
├── 02-backend/           # Backend services and APIs
├── 03-shared-services/   # Shared Python libraries
├── helm/                 # Helm charts for deployment
├── CHANGELOG.md
├── CONTRIBUTING.md
├── LICENSE
├── MAINTAINERS.md
├── SECURITY.md
├── SUPPORT.md
└── publiccode.yml
```

## 01-frontend — Micro Frontend Architecture

A Module Federation architecture built with React, TypeScript, Vite, and the Carbon Design System. A shell application orchestrates multiple independently deployable micro frontends (MFEs) via a shared component library.

The `shell/` subdirectory is the host application (routing, layout, navigation). The root of `01-frontend/` contains the workspace configuration and shared tooling.

| Directory | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `shell/` | Shell application: Module Federation host — routing, layout, navigation, and MFE orchestration |
| `mfe1/` | Template micro frontend: scaffold for creating new MFEs with Module Federation, Zustand, and dual sidebar layout |
| `mfe-ewm/` | Micro frontend: Einwendungsmanagement (objection management) |
| `mfe-fp/` | Micro frontend: Formelle Prüfung (formal review) — document database and PDF review |
| `mfe-kp/` | Micro frontend: Kohärenzprüfung (coherence review) — consistency checks with LLM transparency views |
| `mfe-mp/` | Micro frontend: Materielle Prüfung (substantive review) — norm-chain analysis and subsumption |
| `mfe-verwaltungsakt/` | Micro frontend: Verwaltungsakt — Bescheid generation, procedure configuration, and text editing |
| `mfe-vp/` | Micro frontend: Vollständigkeitsprüfung (completeness check) — verification of application document completeness |
| `mfe-ws/` | Micro frontend: Dokumentenschwärzung (document redaction) — AI-assisted redaction suggestions and PDF export |
| `nginx-config/` | Nginx configuration routing the shell and all MFEs through a single port |
| `shared/` | Shared component library, utilities, styling, and i18n |

See [`01-frontend/README.md`](01-frontend/README.md) for setup and development instructions.

## 02-backend — Backend Services

Independent FastAPI services, each responsible for a distinct domain. All services are Python-based and follow the project-wide code standards.

| Directory | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `berichtskonfigurator/` | Configures and generates Bescheide (legal reports) using AI-assisted text generation |
| `demos-einwendungsmanagement/` | AI-assisted processing of Einwendungen and Stellungnahmen in demosplan — clustering, reply generation, and summarization |
| `demospipes/` | Plugin-driven pipeline framework (FastAPI) whose addons register executors and API routers via entry points |
| `demosplan/` | demosplan participation platform for digital objection and statement management (project and addons) |
| `dokumentenaufbereitung-data-service/` | Serves data from the document-preparation module via auto-generated CRUD APIs with dynamic schema reflection |
| `dokumentenaufbereitung-monorepo/` | Document preparation pipeline: PDF upload, parsing, OCR, chunking, extraction, and RabbitMQ fanout |
| `dokumentenpruefung/` | Completeness check (Vollständigkeitsprüfung) for submitted documents |
| `dokumentenschwaerzung-orchestrator/` | Orchestrates document redaction workflows |
| `dokumentenschwaerzung-pdf-pii-detector/` | Detects and redacts PII in PDF documents using NER |
| `dokumentensuche/` | AI-powered document search, filtering, and analysis |
| `fristenmanagement/` | Deadline management for formal administrative processes |
| `graph-api/` | Knowledge-graph service (FastAPI + Neo4j) for German legal data — laws, paragraphs, and relationships |
| `ki-guv-ai-testing/` | Persistence and aggregation of AI test results, streamed to a testing dashboard |
| `ki-guv-explainability/` | Automated scoring and decision-sequence tracing for AI-generated legal outputs |
| `ki-guv-feedback/` | Collects and analyzes user feedback with Bayesian deterioration detection |
| `kommentar-service/` | Context-based comment management, keyed by tab and author |
| `nachforderungen/` | Manages follow-up requests (Nachforderungen) on regulatory proposals |
| `ner-extraction/` | Named Entity Recognition extraction API |
| `norm-matching/` | Identifies applicable German legal norms via LLM, graph database, and vector search |
| `rechtsquellenvorbereitung/` | Automated extraction and preparation of German legal sources with LLM-powered extraction |
| `request-proxy/` | Auditing reverse proxy for Pharia AI / LLM calls, with full request/response logging |
| `risikohinweis-service/` | AI-powered legal risk assessment (definitions, discretionary powers, norm collisions) |
| `subsumtion-service/` | LLM-powered legal subsumption against German administrative-law norms |
| `tatbestandsmerkmalsextraction/` | Extracts legal elements (Tatbestandsmerkmale) and consequences (Rechtsfolgen) from legal paragraphs |
| `tex2pdf-service/` | HTML-to-PDF/HTML conversion service using Typst or Chromium renderers |
| `xoev-adapter/` | Bidirectional XÖV XML (XPlanung, XTrasse, XBeteiligung) ↔ Mirror-JSON adapter with validation |

Each service has its own README with setup, configuration, and API documentation.

## 03-shared-services — Shared Libraries

Reusable Python packages consumed across backend services.

| Directory | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `bizlog/` | Structured, auditable business-event logging with RabbitMQ integration and audit-safe signing |
| `ki-logging/` | Lightweight logging helpers shared across services |
| `ki-validierung/` | Validation and evaluation framework — scoring, LLM-as-a-judge, explainability, and feedback utilities |
| `prompt-loader/` | Multilingual YAML prompt loader; standardises prompt authoring and produces audit metadata for every LLM call |
| `prompt-security/` | Prompt injection mitigation utilities (OWASP LLM01) for LLM-powered legal decision services |

## helm — Deployment Charts

Helm charts for deploying the full stack to Kubernetes. See the charts directory for per-component values files and deployment documentation.

## Contributing

Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening pull requests.

# Deployment Guide

Minimal steps to build and run the monorepo services locally using Docker.

## Prerequisites

| Tool   | Version | Purpose                          |
|--------|---------|----------------------------------|
| Docker | 24+     | Container builds (BuildKit)      |
| uv     | 0.4+    | Python dependency management     |
| Node   | 20+     | Frontend builds (`npm ci`)       |
| Python | 3.12    | Backend services                 |

## Monorepo Structure

```
01-frontend/          # React frontend (npm workspace, build main Dockerfile)
02-backend/           # Python backend services (one Dockerfile each)
  demospipes/         # Pipeline framework (base + addon images)
03-shared-services/   # Shared Python libraries used by backends
helm/                 # Helm charts (for Kubernetes deployments)
```

## Replacing Base Images

All Dockerfiles use `<CONTAINER_REGISTRY>` as a placeholder for the original private container registry.
Replace these references with public equivalents before building:

| Placeholder in Dockerfile                                            | Public replacement (example)                                      |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| `<CONTAINER_REGISTRY>/astral-uv-python-3.12-bookworm:1.0.0`         | `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.12-bookworm`               |
| `<CONTAINER_REGISTRY>/python-3.12-bookworm:1.0.0`                   | `python:3.12-bookworm`                                    |
| `<CONTAINER_REGISTRY>/uv:0.9.30-python3.12-bookworm-slim-<hash>`    | `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.9.30-python3.12-bookworm-slim`   |

Apply with `sed` across all Dockerfiles:

```bash
find . -name 'Dockerfile*' -exec sed -i \
  -e 's|<CONTAINER_REGISTRY>/astral-uv-python-3.12-bookworm:1.0.0|ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.12-bookworm|g' \
  -e 's|<CONTAINER_REGISTRY>/python-3.12-bookworm:1.0.0|python:3.12-bookworm|g' \
  -e 's|<CONTAINER_REGISTRY>/uv:0\.9\.30-python3\.12-bookworm-slim-[a-f0-9]*|ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.9.30-python3.12-bookworm-slim|g' \
  {} +
```

## Other Placeholders

The export process replaces internal references with placeholders. You may encounter these in configuration files and source code:

| Placeholder         | Meaning                                           | Action required                               |
|---------------------|---------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| `<REDACTED>`        | Internal URL or domain                            | Replace with your own domain or `localhost`   |
| `<LLM_MODEL>`       | LLM model name                                    | Replace with the model name you serve         |
| `<INTERNAL_URL>`    | Internal Kubernetes service URL                   | Replace with your service endpoint            |
| `<ALLOWED_ORIGIN>`  | CORS-allowed origin domain                        | Replace with your frontend URL                |

## Building Backend Services

Each backend service under `02-backend/` has its own Dockerfile. Services depend on shared libraries in `03-shared-services/`, which must be accessible during the Docker build.

```bash
# Example: build a single backend service
cd 02-backend/dokumentenpruefung
DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build -t dokumentenpruefung .
```

**Path dependencies:** Backend Dockerfiles expect `03-shared-services/` to be reachable via relative paths. If `docker build` fails because of missing path dependencies, either:

1. Use the monorepo root as the build context and point `-f` to the service Dockerfile:
   ```bash
   docker build -f 02-backend/dokumentenpruefung/Dockerfile .
   ```
2. Copy the required shared libraries into the service directory before building.

**Build secrets:** Some Dockerfiles use `--mount=type=secret` for private registry credentials. When building with the public base images listed above, pass dummy values:

```bash
DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build \
  --secret id=TECHNICAL_USER_USERNAME,env=DUMMY_USER \
  --secret id=TECHNICAL_USER_TOKEN,env=DUMMY_TOKEN \
  -t my-service .
